intro: Four modules follow the Generative AI Leader exam guide's sections and weights. Each combines a study guide, exam tips, key terms, visual slides, and a narrated lesson. Google renamed Vertex AI to Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform in April 2026; lessons use the new names and mention the old ones.

modules.title: Fundamentals of gen AI
modules.summary: Define core AI and gen AI concepts, learning types, and the ML lifecycle; understand data types and quality; know the layers of the gen AI landscape; and match Google's foundation models (Gemini, Gemma, Imagen, Veo) to use cases.

guide.html: Section 1 is about 30% of the Generative AI Leader exam. It's aimed at leaders, so it tests understanding and business judgment rather than coding.

AI is the broad field; machine learning learns from data; natural language processing works with human language; generative AI creates new content. Foundation models are large models trained on broad data and adapted to many tasks. LLMs are foundation models for language, multimodal models handle several data types, and diffusion models generate images and video. Learning types are supervised (labeled data), unsupervised (finding structure), and reinforcement (learning from rewards). The ML lifecycle runs data ingestion, preparation, training, deployment, and management, and Google Cloud has tools for each stage.

Data quality depends on completeness, consistency, relevance, availability, cost, and format. Structured data fits tables (sales records). Unstructured data is text, images, audio, and video (emails, call recordings). Labeled data has known answers for training; unlabeled data doesn't. Poor data leads to poor or biased output.

guide.h: The gen AI landscape and Google's models
guide.html: Think in layers: infrastructure (compute like TPUs and GPUs), models, platforms (tools to build and manage), agents (systems that reason and use tools), and applications (what end users touch). Google's models: Gemini (multimodal, Google's most capable family), Gemma (lightweight open models you can run and customize yourself), Imagen (text-to-image), and Veo (video generation). Choose a model by modality, context window, security, availability and reliability, cost, performance, and customization options.

tips: Pick the model by modality first, then cost and performance.
Gemma = open and lightweight; Gemini = flagship multimodal.
Imagen makes images; Veo makes video.
Data quality: complete, consistent, relevant, available.
Know the five landscape layers in order.
terms: Large model trained on broad data, adaptable to many tasks.
Able to process several data types, such as text, images, audio, and video.
Generates images or video by gradually removing noise.
How much input a model can consider at once.

slides.title: Gen AI fundamentals
script: Welcome to the gen AI fundamentals module. This section of the Generative AI Leader exam tests whether you understand the concepts and can make sound business choices.

slides.title: Core concepts
script: Artificial intelligence is the broad field, machine learning learns from data, and generative AI creates new content. Foundation models are trained broadly and adapted to many tasks.
Supervised learning uses labeled data, unsupervised learning finds patterns, and reinforcement learning learns from rewards.

slides.title: Data quality and types
script: Good results start with good data: complete, consistent, relevant, available, affordable, and in a usable format.
Structured data fits tables, unstructured data includes text, images, and audio, and labeled data has known answers.

slides.title: Google's foundation models
script: Gemini is Google's most capable multimodal family. Gemma is a lightweight open model family you can run and customize yourself.
Imagen generates images from text, and Veo generates video. Choose by modality, context window, cost, performance, and customization.

Then try the fundamentals question set.

modules.title: Google Cloud's gen AI offerings
modules.summary: Explain Google Cloud's AI strengths and infrastructure; match prebuilt offerings (Gemini app, Gemini Enterprise, Gemini for Google Workspace, Customer Engagement Suite) to needs; and know developer tools on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, RAG offerings, and agent tooling.

guide.html: Section 2 is the largest, about 35% of the exam. In April 2026 Google renamed Vertex AI to Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform ("Agent Platform"), and Vertex AI Search is now Agent Search. Expect both old and new names in study materials.

Google emphasizes an AI-first approach, an enterprise-ready platform (responsible, secure, private, reliable, scalable), AI integrated across its products, and an open approach that supports Google, partner, and open models. Its AI-optimized infrastructure includes the AI Hypercomputer, custom TPUs, GPUs, and global data centers. The platform keeps customers in control of their data and makes AI accessible with low-code and no-code tools, pre-trained models, and APIs.

Gemini app (with Gems, custom versions of Gemini for repeated tasks) helps individuals. Gemini Enterprise brings AI assistance, multimodal search across company data, and custom agents to the whole organization. Gemini for Google Workspace adds AI to Gmail, Docs, Sheets, Slides, and Meet. For customer experience: Agent Search (enterprise search on Agent Platform), Google Search grounding, and the Customer Engagement Suite: Conversational Agents, Agent Assist (helps human agents live), Conversational Insights (analytics), and Contact Center as a Service.

Developers use Agent Platform with Model Garden (catalog of Google, partner, and open models), Agent Search, and AutoML for custom models without heavy coding. RAG options include prebuilt RAG with Agent Search and RAG APIs. Agents use tools (extensions, functions, data stores, plugins) to act. Supporting services include Cloud Storage, databases, Cloud Functions, Cloud Run, and pre-built APIs: Speech-to-Text, Text-to-Speech, Translation, Document Translation, Document AI, Cloud Vision, Video Intelligence, and Natural Language. Use Google AI Studio for quick prototyping with Gemini, and Agent Studio on Agent Platform for enterprise-grade agent building and deployment.

tips: Gemini app = individuals; Gemini Enterprise = organization-wide.
Workspace users get Gemini inside Gmail, Docs, and Meet.
Agent Assist helps human contact-center agents in real time.
Model Garden = catalog of models on Agent Platform.
AI Studio for prototyping; Agent Studio for enterprise agents.
terms: Google Cloud's AI development platform (formerly Vertex AI).
Enterprise search and prebuilt RAG (formerly Vertex AI Search).
Catalog of Google, partner, and open models.
Organization-wide AI assistant, search, and agents.
Custom versions of Gemini for repeated tasks.
Conversational Agents, Agent Assist, Conversational Insights, and CCaaS.

slides.title: Google Cloud's gen AI offerings
script: Welcome to the Google Cloud offerings module, the largest section of the exam. It goes from ready-made AI for employees to tools developers use to build agents.
In April 2026, Vertex AI became Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, and Vertex AI Search became Agent Search.

slides.title: Why Google Cloud
script: Google highlights an AI-first approach, an enterprise-ready platform that is secure and private, and an open ecosystem supporting Google, partner, and open models.
Its infrastructure includes custom TPUs, GPUs, and the AI Hypercomputer, with low-code tools and APIs that make AI accessible.

slides.title: Prebuilt offerings
script: The Gemini app helps individuals, and Gems save custom instructions for repeated tasks. Gemini Enterprise brings assistance, search across company data, and custom agents to the whole organization.
Gemini for Google Workspace adds AI to Gmail, Docs, Sheets, Slides, and Meet.

slides.title: Customer experience
bullets: Agent Search and Google Search grounding

The Customer Engagement Suite includes Conversational Agents, Agent Assist for human agents, Conversational Insights for analytics, and Contact Center as a Service.

slides.title: Building on Agent Platform
bullets: RAG with Agent Search or APIs

Agents use tools such as functions, extensions, and data stores, plus APIs like Document AI, Vision, Speech, and Translation. Prototype in Google AI Studio, and build enterprise agents in Agent Studio.

modules.title: Techniques to improve gen AI model output
modules.summary: Overcome model limitations with grounding, RAG, prompt engineering, fine-tuning, and human oversight; use prompting techniques from zero-shot to ReAct; and tune sampling parameters like temperature and top-p.

guide.html: Section 3 is about 20% of the exam: overcoming foundation model limitations, prompt engineering, and grounding.

Common limitations: data dependency, knowledge cutoff, bias and fairness issues, hallucinations, and edge cases. Google-recommended fixes: grounding, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), prompt engineering, fine-tuning, and human in the loop. Keep improving with continuous monitoring and evaluation: automatic model upgrades, KPIs, security patches, versioning, performance tracking, drift monitoring, and Agent Platform Feature Store.

Zero-shot gives no examples; one-shot gives one; few-shot gives several. Role prompting assigns a persona. Prompt chaining breaks a task into linked prompts. Advanced: chain-of-thought asks for step-by-step reasoning, and ReAct (reason and act) interleaves reasoning with tool use.

Grounding ties output to verifiable sources: first-party enterprise data, third-party data, or world data. Google's options: prebuilt RAG with Agent Search, RAG APIs, and grounding with Google Search. Sampling settings: temperature (randomness), top-p (nucleus sampling), token count and output length, and safety settings (content thresholds).

tips: Hallucinations and knowledge cutoff → grounding or RAG.
Change tone or format → prompt engineering; change behavior deeply → fine-tuning.
Few-shot = examples; chain-of-thought = reasoning; ReAct = reasoning plus tools.
Grounding with Google Search for current world facts.
Lower temperature for factual, consistent answers.
terms: Connecting model output to verifiable data sources.
Retrieving relevant data and adding it to the prompt.
People review or approve model outputs.
Breaking a task into a sequence of linked prompts.
Prompting that interleaves reasoning steps with actions or tool calls.
Samples from the smallest set of tokens whose probabilities add up to p.
The date after which a model has no training data.

slides.title: Improving model output
script: Welcome to the improving output module. It covers why foundation models fall short and the techniques Google recommends to get better, safer results.

slides.title: Limitations and fixes
script: Foundation models depend on their training data, stop at a knowledge cutoff, can be biased, and can hallucinate.
Google recommends grounding, RAG, prompt engineering, fine-tuning, and human in the loop, plus ongoing monitoring for drift.

slides.title: Prompting techniques
script: Zero-shot gives no examples, one-shot gives one, and few-shot gives several. Role prompting assigns a persona, and prompt chaining links steps.
Chain-of-thought asks the model to reason step by step, and ReAct combines reasoning with actions such as tool calls.

slides.title: Grounding and sampling settings
bullets: Agent Search · RAG APIs · Google Search
script: Grounding connects answers to trusted data, from your own enterprise data to Google Search for world facts.
Sampling settings control behavior: temperature for randomness, top-p for nucleus sampling, length limits, and safety thresholds.

slides.title: Review: improving output
script: You've finished the improving output overview. Practice matching each limitation to the right fix and each task to a prompting technique.
Then try the improving output question set.

modules.title: Business strategies for a successful gen AI solution
modules.summary: Choose and implement gen AI solutions for business needs, measure impact, secure AI with SAIF and Google Cloud security tools, and apply responsible AI: privacy, bias, accountability, and explainability.

guide.html: Section 4 is about 15% of the exam: implementing transformational gen AI solutions, secure AI, and responsible AI in business.

Solution types include text, image, and code generation and personalized experiences. Choose based on business requirements and technical constraints such as data, budget, skills, and latency. Integration steps typically are: identify high-value use cases, build a cross-functional team, prepare data, pilot, measure, then scale with change management. Measure impact with KPIs tied to the goal, such as productivity, cost savings, revenue, customer satisfaction, and adoption.

Secure AI protects AI systems from attacks and misuse across the whole ML lifecycle: data, training, deployment, and use. Google's Secure AI Framework (SAIF) extends security foundations to AI, automates defenses, aligns controls, adapts with feedback, and contextualizes risk in business processes. Google Cloud tools: secure-by-design infrastructure, Identity and Access Management (IAM), Security Command Center, and workload monitoring.

Responsible AI and transparency build trust. Privacy risks are reduced with anonymization (removing identity) and pseudonymization (replacing identifiers with tokens). Data quality affects bias and fairness. Accountability means people own AI outcomes, and explainability means decisions can be understood and questioned.

tips: Start with a high-value use case and a pilot, then scale.
Measure with KPIs tied to the business goal.
SAIF = Google's framework for securing AI.
Anonymization removes identity; pseudonymization replaces it with a token.
IAM controls who can use AI resources.
terms: Google's Secure AI Framework for protecting AI systems.
Google Cloud's security and risk management service.
Identity and Access Management: who can do what.
Removing data that identifies a person.
Key performance indicator used to measure impact.
Ability to understand why an AI system produced a result.
Helping people adopt new tools and processes.

slides.title: Business strategy for gen AI
script: Welcome to the business strategy module. It covers how leaders choose, roll out, secure, and govern generative AI solutions.

slides.title: Implementing gen AI
script: Pick a solution that fits business requirements and technical constraints such as data, budget, skills, and latency. Start with a high-value use case and a pilot.
Measure impact with KPIs like productivity, cost savings, revenue, satisfaction, and adoption, then scale with change management.

slides.title: Secure AI and SAIF
script: Secure AI protects systems from attacks and misuse from data to deployment. Google's Secure AI Framework extends security foundations to AI and automates defenses.
Use IAM to control access, Security Command Center to manage risk, and monitoring to watch workloads.

slides.title: Responsible AI in business
script: Responsible AI requires transparency, attention to data quality and bias, and privacy protections such as anonymization and pseudonymization.
People must remain accountable for AI outcomes, and decisions should be explainable.
